transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-08-11 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Chen, Marco Rivera (Redwood); Priya Patel, Daniel Green, Aisha Mohammed (Verdant Labs)

[00:00] Sofia Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining the weekly sync, hope you all had a good week. quick agenda: review results from the integration tests, walk through the SDK tool-calls example that Marco updated, and then structured output for the product summary use-case. any additions?

[00:20] Priya Patel: sounds good, want to start with the odd results we saw in the summarization endpoint — some fields were missing in the JSON output intermittently.

[00:35] Marco Rivera: yeah I saw that, so I dug into the logs. it's typically when the model response exceeded the token window and we had partial generation; the SDK returns the partial structured object which sometimes breaks your upstream parser. I've got a couple of mitigations — one is a required schema validation step, the other is forcing model to return complete object or emit explicit "incomplete": true flag.

[01:05] Aisha Mohammed: ok, so concretely for the SDK — is there a way to get a single atomic object back? our current lambda expects a full JSON with fields title/body/score.

[01:20] Marco Rivera: yes, with the SDK you can use the structured_output helper — it's in the snippet I pushed yesterday. basically you pass a schema definition (we support JSON Schema-lite) and set response_mode: "strict_complete"; if the model can't satisfy it within the token limit the SDK will return an error-type with partial payload and a validation flag. we also have retry/backoff built in for short bursts.

[01:50] Daniel Green: we noticed retries caused duplicate downstream writes. any suggestions?

[02:05] Sofia Chen: that's a common integration issue — idempotency keys. Marco, we should add an example demonstrating idempotency token generation in the SDK and how to handle partials so they don't double-apply.

[02:25] Marco Rivera: yep I'll add a sample middleware in the snippet. also note we have a streaming mode where you can stitch tokens as they arrive and only commit once the schema validation passes. streaming helps with latency-sensitive flows but requires stronger client-side orchestration.

[03:00] Priya Patel: about the streaming — our frontend team is wary of reassembling partial pieces; they'd prefer a single final call. is that achievable without massive latency penalty?

[03:20] Marco Rivera: depends on batch size and prefix caching. for your traffic profile (you shared 300 req/min peak with short context), we recommended small batching with prefix KV cache enabled. that tends to keep tail latency low. the Dedicated run will give you a more deterministic number.

[03:45] Aisha Mohammed: we ran the SDK integration tests — about 10% of calls returned an extra unexpected field name, like "summry" instead of "summary". looks like model hallucination or tokenization issue. thoughts?

[04:05] Marco Rivera: yeah hallucination of keys is a thing. structured_output plus strict schema will reject those keys; you can also map synonyms in the post-processor. another approach is to bias the model via system prompt to enforce exact keys, e.g., "Return JSON with keys: title, summary, score" and provide an example. but the schema check is the safety net.

[04:40] Priya Patel: that would help. can you show the snippet?

[04:50] Marco Rivera: (screen share noted) here's the JS snippet — Redwood SDK client, call generate({model: 'redwood-large-embed-2', instructions, structured_output: {schema: {...}}, response_mode: 'strict_complete', streaming: false, max_tokens: 512}). then on the client we run validateSchema(response.payload, schema). If invalid and partial, SDK returns error.code = 'STRUCTURE_INCOMPLETE'.

[05:25] Daniel Green: you used 'redwood-large-embed-2' — that's an example; for our POC we used the small-latency variant. any quantization/recommendation differences?

[05:40] Marco Rivera: for your use-case prioritizing latency, the low-latency variant is fine. quantized variants reduce memory and cost but sometimes increase small fuzziness in tokenization; for strict structured outputs we recommend the fp16-ish variant or using our tuned verif models which are optimized for schema compliance. I'll include model profile recommendations in the doc.

[06:10] Aisha Mohammed: we also had a few 503s during high concurrency — appeared to be throttling from the client side. do you have rate-limit headers exposed?

[06:25] Sofia Chen: yes we expose x-rw-rate-limit and remaining headers plus a 429/503 backoff guidance. Marco, is there a recommended client-side token bucket sample?

[06:40] Marco Rivera: I'll add that. also important: set retries with exponential backoff and jitter; the SDK has a builtin policy but you can override it. for the POC we'll send a suggested config tuned to Verdant's traffic pattern.

[07:05] Priya Patel: on security — we need to ensure that function/tool call metadata isn't logged externally and that PII is redacted. last week our security team asked about KMS usage.

[07:20] Sofia Chen: for Hosted POC, logs can be disabled and encryption at rest is via provider KMS; for Dedicated we can support customer-managed KMS and stricter audit logs. we'll attach the SOC2 + encryption doc in the follow-up.

[07:40] Daniel Green: good. back to structured output: some of our use-cases expect nested arrays e.g., recommendations -> [{reason, score, actions}]. does the SDK support nested schemas?

[07:55] Marco Rivera: yes, JSON Schema-lite supports arrays and nested objects. caveat: deeper nested structures can increase chance of partials; we suggest chunking large arrays or returning pointers to subsequent calls via tool-calls. That's where function/tool-calling comes in handy: you can ask model to return a summary and then call a function to materialize the full list in paged pieces.

[08:30] Aisha Mohammed: can you walk through the tool-calling flow? we tried it but callbacks didn't line up with our webhook signature.

[08:45] Marco Rivera: sure — typical flow: generate call returns a tool_call event specifying function name + arguments. the SDK can either auto-invoke your registered handler or return the tool payload to you. in auto-invoke mode we hit your webhook with a signed payload (HMAC) and expect a 200 with function result. the mismatch you saw was because your webhook expects snake_case keys, while the SDK used camelCase. small mapping issue.

[09:20] Priya Patel: ah, that explains it. we'll adjust webhook to accept both.

[09:30] Sofia Chen: Marco, action: include a sample server handler for Node+Python showing signature verification and idempotency.

[09:40] Marco Rivera: noted. I'll include both.

[09:50] Daniel Green: one more thing: cost — do we have a ballpark for host vs dedicated for our projected 150k messages/month?

[10:05] Sofia Chen: early estimate: hosted with caching and batching will be cheaper for small-to-medium volumes, Dedicated becomes cost-effective once you need reserved latency and >500k messages/mo. we'll run numbers after the benchmark and present a TCO comparison.

[10:30] Priya Patel: ok good. technical ask: can we add better logging around structured_output validation failures so we can triage fields faster?

[10:45] Marco Rivera: yes we can emit validation diffs in the debug logs (only enabled on request for privacy). we'll show sample diff output: expected keys vs returned keys, type mismatches, and partial flag with token_count.

[11:10] Aisha Mohammed: great — that's helpful. small nit: the SDK sample we used had promises but our stack is async/await heavy; do you provide modern examples?

[11:25] Marco Rivera: yes, I'll include async/await examples in both JS/TS plus Python asyncio.

[11:40] Sofia Chen: let's recap next steps and owners. Marco to send SDK snippet + server handler + schema examples by Friday (2026-08-13). Verdant (Priya/Aisha) to run a 5k messages benchmark and share logs by 2026-08-20. Sofia to coordinate Dedicated latency run and pricing by 2026-08-18.

[12:10] Daniel Green: sounds good. any blockers on your side?

[12:20] Marco Rivera: none, just getting the sample updated.

[12:30] Priya Patel: we'll start the benchmark tomorrow morning and ping if we hit issues.

[12:40] Sofia Chen: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and I'll put the meeting notes in the CRM.

[12:50] Aisha Mohammed: thanks all.

[13:00] End of meeting
